params.body:
Nothing reaches gentells.com with tags the Gentells Standard does not hold. Posts (`articles`) and trends (`trend_cards`) pass a tagging gate on every projection write, by reconcile and by webhook; what is already published goes through the same gate with a backfill command.

## What the gate does

It reads a pinned copy of **Gentells Standard 0.8.0** (`resources/standard/`, written by `bin/sync-standard.mjs` from the `v0.8.0` tag, commit 1ad429e; `StandardTest` refuses a hand edit). Matching is a port of the standard's `resolveTag` and `matchTerm`; the standard's 234 spelling cases run against the port.

| Outcome | When | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| compliant | every tag is a live term (proposed terms such as the element `gaming` pass, as in the standard's validator) | published as is |
| corrected | a retired id with a replacement (`gen-teens` becomes `ls-teens`, moved to the lifestage column), or a spelling the standard maps to one term (`APAC`, `Gen Z`, an element label) | published with the standard's term, recorded |
| held | a tag that is not a term, a reserved term (`gen-genbeta`), a scheme the class is not tagged with, an element fingerprint outside `rules/elements.json` | not published; a public copy comes down, its row kept in the record |

A held item that was public leaves through the existing full-set delete, so the existing brake (`gentells.max_delete_share`, 50%) still applies: a run that would take most of a set off the site is refused, and the refusal now names the holds. A held item returns as soon as the source sends tags that hold, recorded as `released`.

## The record and the backfill

- `tagging_records` (new table): kind, id, title, outcome, source (reconcile, webhook, backfill), standard version, corrections, problems, tags before and after, and a snapshot of the last public row for anything taken down. The same decision is written once, not on every five-minute reconcile.
- `php artisan gentells:tagging-audit` is a dry run: it writes a Markdown report to `storage/app/private/tagging-audit/` and changes nothing. `--apply` corrects in place, takes held items off the site and writes the records; `--kind=post|trend` limits it. The brake applies per kind and a refused kind writes nothing.
- Trends are rewritten on every reconcile, so they pass the gate within minutes of the deploy without the backfill. Posts are only fetched again when they change; the backfill is what gets the existing posts through.

## After merging

1. Deploy runs the migration (one new table).
2. On the box: `php artisan gentells:tagging-audit` and read the report, the held list first.
3. If the held list is right: `php artisan gentells:tagging-audit --apply`.

The pipeline's live tags could not be read from here, so how many items will be corrected or held in production is not known yet; the dry run answers that. The pipeline already matches regions and cohorts with the standard's rule (pipeline #206, #208), so holds are expected to be rare.

## Tests

22 new tests in `StandardTest`, `TaggingGateTest`, `ProjectionTaggingGateTest` and `TaggingAuditTest`: the pinned copy and its digest, the spelling cases, each outcome, the record de-duplication, the release, the brake, the webhook path, aliases not pointing at a held trend, the dry run, `--apply`, a second pass with nothing left to do, a refused pass. Full suite: 424 tests green, Pint clean, Tailwind lint clean.

## Not in this pull request

- Reports carry no tags on the site, and sources only appear inside a trend's graph; neither has tags for the site to check. Sources are tagged in the pipeline.
- A gate in the Studio, before an editor approves, would stop a post earlier and tell the writer why. That is pipeline work, in another repository.

Design note: `docs/design/tagging-gate.md`.
params.title: Tagging gate: nothing published with tags outside the Gentells Standard
